tasks.short: Collect growth, production and environmental readings and file the accepted log.

steps.what: Collect today's growth and environmental measures.
Walk the sample and read scales, meters and probes.
Type raw readings into the day log.
Flag readings outside the crop range.
Accept or reject each flagged reading.

tasks.design: A form on {OPS_SYSTEM} stores the same fields as a climate-controller export: site, house, lot, measure, unit, time and observer. A check on {DATA_PLATFORM} flags values outside the crop range. The farm manager accepts or rejects each flag, and only that accepted batch stays in the production log that {BI} reads.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings lived on paper and in a workbook, so a dead probe looked like a real drop until someone who knew the house looked.
tasks.enabler_now: A phone form and a controller export can share one field list, and range checks are ordinary code.
tasks.still_hard: A new crop, a changed unit, or a broken sensor still needs someone who knows that house.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a failed probe from real crop stress.

ambition.what: Accept or reject an out-of-range reading the same day for every house, not only at the weekly meeting.

tasks.altitude: Most retyping leaves the week. The manager still walks a sample and still decides which outliers are real. They gain no new right to change the growing plan.

reach.task: Scout the same houses for disease
reach.learn: Which flags are sensor faults and which are the crop

evidence.claim: Range checks on a fixed field list catch impossible values before a person looks. The person still explains the exception.
Storing the observer's name is staff data. National works-council rules may require consent before that name is used to judge the person. The source pack names a Dutch rule; other countries differ.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager owns the accepted production log. Finance does not post from it until a later task. A controller that already runs the climate is system time and is not saved labour.

Structured input: site, house or field, lot, measure, unit, timestamp, observer. Producer is the person on the round or the controller export. If the export is missing, the same fields are typed. A free-text note cannot be the only record.
Upkeep of range rules is extra and is not inside the remaining review time.
unknowns: Which houses already export, and in which fields?
Who may accept a flagged reading when the manager is off?
Is the observer's name used in supervision?
research_questions: What share of flags are sensor faults rather than the crop?
What does the manager do with the hour that retyping used to take?

already_counted.description: Review of flagged readings is already in the accept step.

incremental.description: Keep range rules and units current when a crop or sensor changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If a third of houses stay on paper, the manager retypes those and rechecks every flag. The walk and the outlier decision stay. Provisional, not measured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run the nursery week: what is on the benches, for whom, and what is late.

steps.what: Read orders due and which benches are full.
Set the nursery week list for plants and dispatch.
Pot, space and pick to the week list.
Walk the benches and note what is off the list.
Sign the revised week list before dispatch.

tasks.design: Customer orders already in {CRM} and bench counts in {OPS_SYSTEM} fill a week list. The farm manager still sets potting, spacing and dispatch, walks the benches, and signs the list in {WORKFLOW} before anything leaves. The crew's bench work is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders, bench maps and dispatch sat in different workbooks, so the week was rebuilt by hand every Monday.
tasks.enabler_now: The order list and the bench map can share a lot code, so the week list is a query plus a signature.
tasks.still_hard: A customer who changes a colour or a date still needs a person who can re-cut the week.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which benches can absorb a late order without wrecking the rest.

ambition.what: See which orders are late against the benches every morning, not only at the Monday meeting.

tasks.altitude: Monday rebuild shrinks. The manager still sets the week and still walks. Dispatch cannot leave on an unsigned list.

reach.learn: Which lines the manager has signed and which are still open

evidence.claim: A week list built from orders and stock is a configured query. The choice of what to cut or hold is not a rule.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager signs the week list. The dispatch lead loads only signed lines. Selling terms stay with the buyer conversation in another task.
Structured input: order number, variety, quantity, due date, bench, lot. Producer is the order book and the bench count. Missing bench counts are typed as the same fields.
Crew time on the benches is other people's work and is not saved here.
unknowns: Are orders already one record per line, or a mail thread?
Who may sign the week list when the manager is on another site?
research_questions: How often does a signed list change again the same day?

already_counted.description: Morning review of orders and benches is already in the first step.

incremental.description: Keep variety and bench codes aligned when the catalogue changes.

approvals.approved_version: week list revision the manager signs; a later edit voids it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If orders stay in mail, the morning review barely shrinks. The walk and the crew's bench work stay. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct spawning, egg incubation and fry rearing, and record what happened.

steps.what: Set the spawn window and the handling rules.
Trap breeders and run the spawning and incubation.
Count eggs, losses and fry against the batch.
Decide whether a weak batch is treated or culled.
Post the decision onto the batch record.

tasks.design: The spawn protocol stays a document the farm manager writes. Counts of eggs, losses and fry are fields on the batch in {OPS_SYSTEM}, not a side workbook. The manager still decides treat or cull, and that decision is the only version that posts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hatch books were paper, so a weak batch was noticed late and the reason was a memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Batch, parent stock and daily counts are a fixed field list a form can store.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a batch is diseased or merely slow is still a judgement on the fish in front of you.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees a soft batch early enough to stop it spreading.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconstructing the hatch book and the same time on the fish. Treat-or-cull stays their decision.

reach.task: Run the spawn and the incubators
reach.learn: Which counts the manager trusts and which batches are already decided

evidence.claim: Egg, loss and fry counts are arithmetic on a batch record. The treat-or-cull choice is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager owns the protocol and the treat-or-cull decision. Technicians do the handling. Medicine purchase is a later procurement step.
Structured input: batch, parents, date, egg count, loss count, fry count, water temperature. Producer is the technician on the unit. Missing counts are typed, not guessed.
Technician handling time is not this role's saving.
unknowns: Is there already a batch record, or only a paper hatch book?
Who may cull when the manager is not on site?
research_questions: Which losses repeat for the same parent stock?

already_counted.description: The treat-or-cull decision is already the manager's remaining time.

incremental.description: Update the protocol when a handling rule changes.
Technicians still key in counts the form does not get from a counter.

approvals.approved_version: batch decision text and counts the manager confirmed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If counts stay on paper, only the posting step shrinks. Handling and the cull decision stay. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct the transfer of mature fish and sign the record before they move.

steps.what: Plan which lots move, where, and on which day.
Check water, oxygen and the receiving permit.
Load, move and unload the fish.
Sign the transfer record with counts and losses.
Send the signed record to the receiving site.

tasks.design: The move plan and the permit check stay with the farm manager. Counts and losses are fields on a transfer record in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The notice to the receiving site goes out from {EMAIL} only after the manager has signed that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transfer sheets were filled in after the truck had left, so losses were argued from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: A short form can lock lot, counts, losses and the permit reference before the notice is sent.
tasks.still_hard: Fish condition on the day, and whether the receiving water is fit, are still seen on site.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is the person who can refuse a move when the fish or the water look wrong.
tasks.altitude: Paper after the fact shrinks. The manager still plans the move and can still stop it. They do not gain the right to ignore a permit.

reach.learn: Which transfer record is the signed version

evidence.claim: A transfer record with required fields can block a notice that has no signature. It cannot judge the fish.
Moving live animals can need a permit under national rules. The source pack does not name a fisheries statute, so the permit check stays a person's.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager signs the transfer. The receiving site accepts the lot. Permit rules are national and are not coded here.
Structured input: lot, headcount out, headcount in, losses, water temperature, permit reference, destination. Producer is the technician at load and unload. Missing counts stop the notice.
Driving and handling time belongs to the crew.
unknowns: Which moves need a permit, and where is that document kept?
Does the receiving site already share a lot code?
research_questions: How often is a signed record corrected after the truck arrives?

already_counted.description: The permit check is already remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Keep destination and permit references current.

approvals.approved_version: transfer counts and permit reference the manager signs
the same signed transfer record; a later edit stops the notice

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the crew still phones the numbers in later, the notice is the only sure saving. The move itself stays. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farm manager still walks, still decides outliers, culls, moves and the week list. Retyping and chasing unsigned lists shrink. No new authority over permits or pay.
reach: Crop technicians learn which readings are accepted.
Dispatch loads only a signed week list.
skills_to_grow: Write a field list others can fill.
Say which exceptions they will still judge themselves.
role.ambitious_version: Every house has an accepted log the same day, and a week list that dispatch cannot load unsigned.

job.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
